target.title: fix(clickclack): reply to a top-level message in-channel, not as a new thread
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The ClickClack channel extension delivered **every** agent/gateway reply as a **thread reply**. `sendClickClackText` routed any `replyToId` to `client.createThreadReply()` (`POST /api/messages/{id}/thread/replies`), and `inbound.ts` stamps `replyToId = <triggering message id>` on every reply. So every reply to a top-level channel message opened its own thread — the main channel timeline stayed empty and the chat was practically unusable (each answer was buried in a separate per-message thread pane).

This affects the current default behavior on `main`; there is no config toggle for it.

## Fix

Route a bare `replyToId` (a reply to a top-level message) to the **main channel as a quote-reply** (`quoted_message_id`) instead of opening a thread — matching the reply-to affordance the Discord/Slack/Telegram channels already use. Threads are reserved for genuine thread context: an explicit `threadId` (the inbound message already lived in a thread) or a `thread:`-kind target. DM replies likewise become quote-replies in the same conversation. When there is no reply context, `quoted_message_id` is omitted, so plain sends are byte-for-byte unchanged.

The ClickClack server already accepts `quoted_message_id` on `POST /channels/{id}/messages`, `POST /dms/{id}/messages`, and thread replies (empty is treated as absent), so no server change is needed.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Ran against a live ClickClack server with a bound agent account.

**Before** (stock routing): a user message in a channel produced a reply POSTed to `/api/messages/{id}/thread/replies` — a new thread; the main channel showed nothing.

**After** this change: sending a channel message runs the turn and the reply is delivered to the **main channel** as a quote-reply. Observed on the wire and in the stored rows:

```
# server access log — reply POSTed to the channel, not a thread:
POST /api/channels/{chan}/messages  201     (was: POST /api/messages/{id}/thread/replies)

# stored message rows after the turn (channel timeline, not a thread):
user  seq 30  body "…quote-reply routing check…"           (id = msg_PARENT)
bot   seq 32  quoted_message_id = msg_PARENT  body "🤖 ack — quote-reply routing confirmed."
```

The bot reply lands as a top-level channel message whose `quoted_message_id` points at the message it answers.

### Unit tests

Added `outbound.test.ts` covering the routing decision:
- top-level channel reply → `createChannelMessage` with `quotedMessageId`, `createThreadReply` not called
- no reply context → plain channel message (no quote)
- explicit `threadId` → stays in the thread
- `thread:` target → thread reply
- DM reply → `createDirectMessage` quote-reply

And `http-client.test.ts` cases asserting `quoted_message_id` is included when quoting and omitted otherwise.
